$comment: Curated input to scripts/report-v2-witness-coverage.mjs: the top-20 v2 core obligations with no major-2 witness, ranked security / tenant isolation / idempotency / replay first, then wire shape, then behaviour. `rule` MUST be a verbatim substring of `doc` (whitespace-normalised); the report re-checks it and the section's major-2 citations on every run. Judgement, not derivation: a regex cannot decide which rule a test discharges (RFC 0191).

risks.title: Host storage leaks across tenants
risks.rule: A read for one tenant MUST NOT return data another tenant wrote, even under an identical key or name
risks.today: Major 1 only: `kv-`, `table-`, `blob-` and `cache-cross-tenant-isolation` drive the v1 seam `POST /v1/host/sample/test/surface`. `vectorStore` and `searchIndex` have no isolation leg at any major. No v2 seam exists for host storage.
risks.why: One missing tenant prefix exposes every tenant's data. It covers six families and is the widest isolation rule in core.

scenario.name: v2-storage-cross-tenant-isolation
scenario.gate: each advertised storage family, plus a second-tenant credential (`OPENWOP_TEST_TENANT_B_API_KEY`) and a storage-probe fixture workflow
scenario.asserts: per advertised family, a run under tenant A writes value V at key K, and a run under tenant B reading K on the run surface sees absent / `not_found`, never V
scenario.sabotage: key the store by name only (drop the tenant prefix): tenant B reads V and the leg fails

risks.title: Agent memory crosses tenants
risks.rule: A ref MUST resolve to one tenant's entries, whatever the caller's permissions.
risks.today: Major 1 only (`agentMemoryCrossTenantIsolation`, `memory-attribution-tenant-scoped`). The family is gated at major 2, but no major-2 scenario cites §`memory`.
risks.why: Memory holds conversation content and redacted secrets. A cross-tenant read is a direct data breach.

scenario.name: v2-memory-cross-tenant-isolation
scenario.gate: `memory` advertised, second-tenant credential, the cross-tenant memory fixture
scenario.asserts: a run under tenant B given tenant A's `memoryRef` gets `[]` from `list` and `null` from `get`; a malformed ref (traversal, NUL, oversize) also gets `[]` / `null`
scenario.sabotage: resolve `memoryRef` without checking its tenant: B's run returns A's entry

risks.title: Workspace files cross scopes
risks.rule: MUST derive the scope from the authenticated identity and MUST NOT return or disclose another scope's file
risks.today: Major 1 only (`workspace-cross-tenant-isolation`, through the v1 seam `POST /v1/host/sample/workspace/op`). The v2 seams profile already mounts `/conformance/seams/workspace/files`.
risks.why: Agent workspace files are durable and shared across runs. Taking the scope from a request field instead of the identity lets any caller read any workspace.

scenario.name: v2-workspace-scope-from-identity
scenario.gate: `workspace` advertised, seams profile `openwop-conformance-seams-v2`, second-tenant credential
scenario.asserts: a file written under tenant A through the v2 seam is `404` (or `403`) for tenant B by path and absent from B's list, even when B names A's workspace id in the request
scenario.sabotage: take `workspaceId` from the request body instead of the credential: B reads A's file

risks.title: Queue messages cross tenants
risks.rule: A tenant's consumer MUST NOT receive another tenant's messages, even on the same topic.
risks.today: Major 1 only (`queue-cross-tenant-isolation`, v1 seam).
risks.why: Topics are named by pack authors, so two tenants sharing a pack share topic names by default.

scenario.name: v2-queue-cross-tenant-isolation
scenario.gate: `queueBus` advertised, second-tenant credential, a queue-probe fixture workflow
scenario.asserts: a message published under tenant A on topic T is never consumed by tenant B's consumer on T within the poll window, while A's own consumer receives it (the positive control)
scenario.sabotage: name the physical queue by topic only: B consumes A's message

risks.title: Raw secrets reach events or logs
risks.rule: Raw key material MUST NOT appear in any event, log, trace, prompt, error, export or screenshot
risks.today: Major 1 only, and only on the envelope and OTel paths (`envelope-reasoning-secret-redaction`, `secret-leakage-otel-attribute`). Nothing at major 2 checks the event log, snapshot or error body.
risks.why: This is the BYOK boundary. One leaked provider key in an event log is replicated to every consumer and every fork.

scenario.name: v2-secret-canary-absent
scenario.gate: `secrets` advertised with `resolveInPack`, a canary-secret fixture workflow
scenario.asserts: after a run that resolves a canary secret and then fails, the canary bytes appear nowhere in the event log, the snapshot, the SSE stream, the error envelope or a fork's log
scenario.sabotage: echo the resolved plaintext into `node.completed` outputs: the scan finds the canary

risks.title: A tool runs without its scopes
risks.rule: If one is missing or cannot be evaluated, it MUST NOT invoke, MUST emit `agent.toolReturned` with `status: forbidden`
risks.today: Major 1 only (`tool-hooks-authorization-fail-closed`, through the v1 tool-hooks seam).
risks.why: Per-tool authorization is the only check between an agent and an external side effect. Fail-open here turns a prompt injection into an action.

scenario.name: v2-tool-authorization-fail-closed
scenario.gate: `toolHooks.perToolAuthorization`, a fixture agent whose principal lacks one `requiredScopes` entry
scenario.asserts: the tool is not invoked (the fixture receiver sees no call), the log carries `agent.toolReturned` `status: forbidden`, and the response is `403 forbidden` with `details.scope: "tool"`
scenario.sabotage: treat an unevaluable scope as granted: the receiver sees the call

risks.title: Anonymous callers gain a tool baseline
risks.rule: A host MUST NOT resolve a role, scope or default tool baseline for it, or widen it within a session.
risks.today: Six major-1 scenarios (`anonymous-actor-*`). The only major-2 gate is `v2-mcp-mount-map`, which skips when the family is advertised; no major-2 scenario cites §1.5.
risks.why: An anonymous subject reaches the public internet. Any default grant is a grant to everyone.

scenario.name: v2-anonymous-actor-default-deny
scenario.gate: `anonymousActor` advertised; seam-gated until a public-surface observation path is minted
scenario.asserts: a call to a tool outside the surface allowlist is denied with `authorization.decided` `reason: anon-not-granted` and no dispatch; `listTools` for the subject equals the allowlist exactly
scenario.sabotage: merge the authenticated default toolset into the anonymous grant: the extra tool dispatches

risks.title: A step routes to another subject's runner
risks.rule: A host MUST NOT route a step to a runner its run's subject does not own, and MUST match on subject before capability.
risks.today: Major 1 only (`self-hosted-runner`).
risks.why: A runner holds credentials the host cannot see. Mis-routing sends one user's prompt and tool arguments to another user's machine.

scenario.name: v2-runner-subject-isolation
scenario.gate: `selfHostedRunner` advertised, two harness runners registered under two subjects with identical `dispatchKinds`
scenario.asserts: a run owned by subject A dispatches only to A's runner, and with A's runner gone fails `runner_unavailable` rather than using B's
scenario.sabotage: pick the first runner matching `dispatchKinds`: B's runner receives A's frame

risks.title: Egress reaches private addresses
risks.rule: Before connecting it MUST resolve the target, reject loopback, RFC 1918, link-local and cloud-metadata addresses, and pin the resolved address for the connection
risks.today: Major 1 only, and only the advertisement (`http-client-ssrf` asserts `ssrfGuard: true`; the rejection is left to the host's own tests).
risks.why: SSRF to a cloud-metadata endpoint hands a pack the host's cloud credentials.

scenario.name: v2-safefetch-ssrf-refused
scenario.gate: `httpClient.safeFetch`, a fixture workflow that fetches a URL from its input
scenario.asserts: fetches of `169.254.169.254`, `127.0.0.1`, `10.0.0.1` and a public hostname resolving to loopback each fail `egress_denied` with `reason: ssrf-blocked`, and no connection reaches a harness listener
scenario.sabotage: check the hostname string, not the resolved address: the loopback-resolving hostname connects

risks.title: Pack file access escapes the sandbox root
risks.rule: A path that escapes the root, whether absolute, through `..` segments or through a symlink, MUST be refused.
risks.today: Major 1 only (`fs-path-traversal`, v1 seam `POST /v1/host/sample/fs/read`).
risks.why: Path traversal from pack code reads host configuration and credentials.

scenario.name: v2-fs-sandbox-escape-refused
scenario.gate: `fs` advertised, an fs-probe fixture workflow
scenario.asserts: reads of an absolute path, a `../` path and a symlink out of `sandboxRoot` each fail `forbidden` with `details.reason: path-outside-sandbox`; a read inside the root succeeds
scenario.sabotage: normalise `..` but follow symlinks: the symlink read succeeds

risks.title: Query injection through host storage
risks.rule: `nosql` filter operators MUST NOT permit injection. Server-side script evaluation, such as MongoDB `$where`, MUST be refused unless an explicit allowlist is configured.
risks.today: `sql` has a major-1 leg (`sql-injection-rejection`); `nosql` has no leg at any major.
risks.why: Operator injection bypasses tenant filters and reads every document in a collection.

scenario.name: v2-storage-injection-refused
scenario.gate: `sql` or `nosql` advertised, a query-probe fixture workflow
scenario.asserts: a `nosql` filter carrying `$where` is refused `forbidden`; a `sql` query whose user value holds `' OR 1=1 --` returns only the bound row
scenario.sabotage: pass filter objects to the driver unvalidated: `$where` executes

risks.title: An import carries credential values
risks.rule: A host MUST reject with `422` an imported bundle whose payload carries a literal credential value.
risks.today: Major 1 only (`export-bundle-portability`, v1 seam `/v1/host/sample/import`).
risks.why: An export bundle crosses tenants and hosts by design. Accepting literal credentials launders secrets across that boundary.

scenario.name: v2-import-refuses-credential-literal
scenario.gate: `portability.import`
scenario.asserts: a dry-run and a real import of a bundle whose `connection-ref` carries a literal token each answer `422`, and the dry run writes nothing (a follow-up read finds no created entity)
scenario.sabotage: strip unknown fields instead of refusing: the import returns `200`

risks.title: Unverified inbound events start runs
risks.rule: A failed `required` check starts no run and dead-letters only that delivery. A refused event MUST NOT change the subscription's state or emit `trigger.subscription-state-changed`
risks.today: Major 1 only (`trigger-ingestion`, `trigger-bridge-delivery`, `trigger-refused-event-keeps-subscription`). The section is attributed to `webhooks` by document name; its obligations belong to `triggerBridge`.
risks.why: An unsigned inbound event that starts a run lets anyone on the internet trigger workflows with chosen input, and one that dead-letters the subscription lets them disable a working integration with a single post.

scenario.name: v2-trigger-ingestion-verification
scenario.gate: `triggerBridge.ingestion` with a `required` verification source
scenario.asserts: an event with a bad signature starts no run and dead-letters only that delivery; the subscription stays `active` with no state-change event; the same event correctly signed then starts exactly one run
scenario.sabotage: log the verification failure and deliver anyway: a run starts; or dead-letter the subscription: the signed event is refused

risks.title: Front-end plugins load unsigned
risks.rule: MUST verify the pack signature before loading, failing closed
risks.today: Major 1 only (`frontend-plugin-packs`). The v2 seams profile already serves test packs with `.sig` files under `/conformance/seams/packs-test/`.
risks.why: A plugin bundle runs in the user's browser next to the host UI. An unsigned bundle is arbitrary script.

scenario.name: v2-frontend-plugin-signature-required
scenario.gate: `uiPlugins` advertised, seams profile (packs-test registry)
scenario.asserts: installing a `frontend-plugin` pack with a tampered `.sig` is refused and the pack never appears as installed; the correctly signed pack installs
scenario.sabotage: skip verification when the signature file is missing or unreadable: the tampered pack installs

risks.title: Replay re-resolves approver membership
risks.rule: Approver eligibility recorded on a resume event is fixed history; a host MUST NOT re-resolve membership during replay.
risks.today: No witness at any major. `v2-approver-enforced` checks live enforcement, not replay.
risks.why: A replay that re-checks membership against today's roster rewrites who approved what, and breaks audit.

scenario.name: v2-replay-approver-eligibility-fixed
scenario.gate: `replay` modes include `replay`, `interrupt` approval, a second-tenant or second-subject credential
scenario.asserts: a run approved by subject S, then replayed after S loses membership, completes identically and re-emits the recorded resolution
scenario.sabotage: re-run the eligibility check on replay: the replay parks or fails

risks.title: Replay raises a fresh interrupt
risks.rule: `ctx.interrupt(K)` MUST short-circuit to the persisted `interrupt.resolved`, raising no new `interrupt.requested`.
risks.today: No major-2 witness. The section has no major-2 citation.
risks.why: A replay that re-asks a human repeats approvals and can take a different branch than the source.

scenario.name: v2-replay-interrupt-short-circuit
scenario.gate: `replay` modes include `replay`, `interrupt` advertised
scenario.asserts: replaying a resolved approval run emits no `interrupt.requested` after the fork point, reaches the same terminal and carries the source's resolve value
scenario.sabotage: re-execute `ctx.interrupt` on replay: the run parks in `waiting-approval`

risks.title: Replay divergence goes unreported
risks.rule: MUST emit `replay.diverged` `{ originalEventId, replayEventId, divergencePoint }`;
risks.today: No scenario at any major asserts `replay.diverged`. Only its refusal variant has a major-1 leg (`replay-divergence-at-refusal`).
risks.why: Divergence is how a replay user learns the replay is not the source run. Silent divergence makes replay evidence worthless.

scenario.name: v2-replay-divergence-emitted
scenario.gate: `replay` modes include `replay`, the mock-AI seam (a scripted response that differs on replay)
scenario.asserts: the replay continues, emits `replay.diverged` naming both event ids and a `divergencePoint`, and reaches a terminal
scenario.sabotage: substitute the recorded output silently: no `replay.diverged` appears

risks.title: Inbound dedup starts a second run
risks.rule: with `dedup`, MUST answer a `dedupKey` repeated within retention (at least 24 hours) with the prior `runId`;
risks.today: Major 1 only (`trigger-bridge-delivery`).
risks.why: Sources redeliver. Without dedup one upstream event runs a workflow, and its side effects, twice.

scenario.name: v2-trigger-dedup-prior-run
scenario.gate: `triggerBridge.dedup`
scenario.asserts: two deliveries with the same `dedupKey` yield one run, and the second answer carries the first `runId`
scenario.sabotage: dedup in memory only and restart between deliveries (or skip dedup): a second run starts

risks.title: Production keys can force the engine version
risks.rule: Servers MUST reject it on production API keys with `403 force_engine_version_forbidden`.
risks.today: No family: `headers.md` homes none. `version-fold` (major 1) holds one API key and cannot tell a production key from a test key, so the refusal is never exercised.
risks.why: Forcing an old engine version on production traffic reopens fixed behaviour on live runs.

scenario.name: v2-force-engine-version-production-refused
scenario.gate: a production-class key supplied to the harness (new env, e.g. `OPENWOP_TEST_PRODUCTION_API_KEY`)
scenario.asserts: `POST /runs` with `OpenWOP-Force-Engine-Version` on the production key answers `403 force_engine_version_forbidden` and creates no run
scenario.sabotage: honour the header on any key: the run is created

risks.title: Residency constraints are accepted and ignored
risks.rule: A host advertising `dataResidency` MUST honor-or-reject, and MUST NOT silently accept-and-ignore:
risks.today: Major 1 only (`data-residency-admission`).
risks.why: A silently ignored residency constraint puts regulated data in the wrong jurisdiction while the client believes otherwise.

scenario.name: v2-residency-honor-or-reject
scenario.gate: `dataResidency` advertised
scenario.asserts: a run naming a region outside `dataResidency.regions` is refused `residency_unavailable`; one naming an advertised region is accepted
scenario.sabotage: drop the `residency` field during validation: the unadvertised region is accepted
